decision_reason: CNR developed and operates this exact attendance system, and its source is public and actively maintained. Hold because the first-party license evidence conflicts on the license family: the full root LICENSE is GNU GPL version 3, while the README and publiccode.yml claim GNU Affero GPL 3.0-or-later. Both are OSI-approved, but whether the network-source AGPL grant applies cannot be stated precisely from these conflicting declarations.

government_provenance.note: CNR's IIT-hosted product page identifies ePAS as developed by IIT-CNR with CNR ICT and personnel offices, operated at CNR headquarters, integrated with CNR systems, and distributed to CNR institutes/units. This is specific CNR authorship and stewardship, not merely third-party government use.

public_source.note: The canonical public repository contains the application source, developer/install documentation, deployment files, and user-facing product description without credentials; its README maps this source to the CNR ePAS service.

eligible_license.note: The full root file is GNU General Public License version 3; the same repository's README badge and license prose say GNU Affero General Public License, and publiccode.yml declares AGPL-3.0-or-later. These are both OSI-approved but not the same grant. The README points to this conflicting LICENSE file, so exact applicable terms and scope remain unresolved.

primary_evidence.note: The official CNR ePAS deployment exposes its current application information/privacy page. CNR's product page documents production operation, user functionality, support/training, and over 100 institute installations; CNR unit documentation also names ePAS in current attendance administration.

product_identity: ePAS (Electronic Personnel Attendance System), the CNR web application for staff attendance, absences, schedules, and monthly attendance attestations
agency: Consiglio Nazionale delle Ricerche (CNR), developed by Istituto di Informatica e Telematica (IIT) with CNR ICT and personnel offices
geography: National CNR service, Italy; CNR headquarters in Rome and IIT development in Pisa
license: Unresolved between GPL-3.0-only (full root LICENSE text) and AGPL-3.0-or-later (README/publiccode.yml claim); both are OSI-approved, but the exact network-source obligation cannot be attributed confidently to the full first-party code scope
family_note: Review covers the assigned CNR ePAS monolith repository and its stated CNR attendance-system identity. The source has later ePAS integration/service repositories; do not infer their code/license scope from this repository without checking those components separately.
status_note: The root LICENSE first appears with public source on 2021-03-03; the repository had substantive feature/documentation changes through 2026-09-09, and the official CNR service endpoint remains online. The 2026 publiccode releaseDate was not used as the open-source year. Hold is solely for the conflicting GPL-versus-AGPL first-party declarations.

decision_reason: CNR's first-party software record identifies the CNR Parco Auto application and CNR maintenance, its public repository contains the full application and AGPL-3.0-or-later grant, and CNR's mandatory-use circular/user manual plus 2025 planning documents establish operational use and continued platform work. The service is currently distributed at the CNR host and the source contains recent application changes.

government_provenance.note: The CNR repository's publiccode record identifies Parco Auto, gives the CNR public-body code and CNR internal maintainer contact; CNR's official 2023 circular separately names the CNR-Parco Auto application and requires its use by all CNR structures.

public_source.note: The canonical public repository contains the Angular/Java web application source, build/deployment files, documentation, and a user manual without credentials; the linked CNR production service corresponds to the product named in this repository.

eligible_license.note: The root file contains the full GNU Affero General Public License v3 text and the first-party publiccode.yml states AGPL-3.0-or-later for the repository software. This grant is scoped to the CNR project source; framework/dependency code is separately licensed and is not being represented as authored under this grant.

primary_evidence.note: CNR's General Directorate Circular 35/2023 identifies CNR-Parco Auto, makes entry/update of fleet data mandatory for CNR structures, and attaches the operating manual. CNR's 2025–2027 PIAO includes implementation and feature/user-instruction work for the platform, and the official production service remains live.

product_identity: CNR Parco Auto, the CNR fleet-management application for recording and maintaining institutional vehicle data
agency: Consiglio Nazionale delle Ricerche (CNR), including its General Directorate as operational sponsor
geography: National CNR service, Italy; administered from CNR headquarters in Rome
license: AGPL-3.0-or-later for first-party Parco Auto source in this repository; third-party dependencies retain their own grants

status_note: The first root LICENSE/source commit is dated 2020-10-30; the latest observed functional application commits are 2025-06-20, with repository maintenance/publiccode validation changes in May 2026. The live CNR service and 2025–2027 CNR plan support current distribution/use. publiccode.yml releaseDate was not treated as the source year.

decision_reason: CNR created and owns SIGLA and the repository is public under an AGPL-3.0-or-later first-party grant. Hold because direct official sources document CNR's transition away from SIGLA beginning in 2025 and ISIN's earlier move to another system; although the official SIGLA host still serves the application shell and source changes continued through November 2025, I could not verify which agency currently operates the exact repository version or substantiate the publiccode.yml usedBy claims for ISS. Current primary-use/source correspondence therefore remains unresolved.

government_provenance.note: The first-party CNR README calls SIGLA CNR-owned and says it was designed in response to CNR's accounting requirements; publiccode.yml identifies internal CNR maintenance and CNR as the product's public-body owner. This is government creation/stewardship, not just third-party use.

public_source.note: The canonical public repository contains the modular Java accounting application, installation/demo instructions, and user/technical documentation without credentials.

eligible_license.note: The root file contains the full GNU Affero General Public License v3 text, the README expressly applies GNU AGPL to SIGLA, and publiccode.yml declares AGPL-3.0-or-later. This grant covers first-party SIGLA source in the assigned repository; JADA/SIOPE+ and other linked dependencies are separate components with their own licensing.

primary_evidence.note: The official CNR circular index links Circular 8/2025 and its manual for the transition from SIGLA to U-GOV; a CNR institute page states central CNR disabled SIGLA from 2025-01-01, while official ISIN records say it selected a new accounting package after CNR stated SIGLA would no longer be used/updated. The official SIGLA host still responds, but that does not prove live production use. Current deployment and exact source parity are unclear; the repo's publiccode.yml usedBy list is metadata, not use proof.

product_identity: SIGLA (Sistema Informativo per la Gestione delle Linee di Attività), CNR's multi-entity accounting and financial-management system for research/public bodies
agency: Consiglio Nazionale delle Ricerche (CNR); CNR is the owner/developer. ISIN and ISS appear in project metadata as adopters, but current use is not independently established.
geography: National CNR system, Italy; CNR headquarters in Rome
license: AGPL-3.0-or-later for first-party SIGLA source in the assigned repository; linked JADA/SIOPE+ and other components retain their separate grants
family_note: The CNR main repository describes SIGLA as a modular system and links separately maintained JADA and SIOPE+ components; this decision covers the named SIGLA product, not those linked components as independently cataloged products. ISIN's 2023 agreement/use was historical and its later migration must not be counted as current reuse.
status_note: The first root LICENSE commit is dated 2019-11-14; latest substantive application change observed is 2025-11-25. On 2026-09-29 the old CNR contab URL redirected to the official sigla.cnr.it host, which still returned the application shell, but CNR's 2025 transition and ISIN's move to URBI leave production status/current use uncertain. The 2025 publiccode releaseDate was not used as the source year.

decision_reason: CNR identifies this source as its Scrivania Digitale workflow product and directly maps its first-party publiccode landing URL to the current CNR service. The repo contains the application and substantial user documentation under AGPL-3.0-or-later; CNR's 2025–2026 operational notices document current use across its offices. Although core-source changes are quieter, the current official deployment and repository landing URL establish source/product correspondence and satisfy the maintained exception.

government_provenance.note: The first-party publiccode metadata describes the product as part of CNR's e-government project, identifies CNR as the public-body code and internal maintainer affiliation, and points its landingURL to the current CNR deployment. CNR's official GitHub organization also identifies this repository as its Scrivania Digitale platform.

public_source.note: The canonical public repository contains the web application source, build/deployment instructions, and a comprehensive workflow/user manual. Its publiccode landingURL is the exact CNR production service domain.

eligible_license.note: The root file contains the full GNU Affero General Public License v3 text and first-party publiccode.yml expressly declares AGPL-3.0-or-later. The grant is scoped to this application's first-party source; its named framework, storage-cloud and other third-party dependencies retain separate grants.

primary_evidence.note: CNR's 2026 mobility-call page says the entire competition process is conducted through the Nuova Scrivania Digitale platform. The CNR portal's May 2025 notice says all institutes/offices/units use the platform for attendance attestations, and CNR's official 2023 Smart Working manual documents user procedures for its workflows.

agency: Consiglio Nazionale delle Ricerche (CNR), developed/maintained through its ICT team
geography: National CNR service, Italy; CNR headquarters in Rome
license: AGPL-3.0-or-later for first-party sprint-flows application code; framework, storage, and other dependencies are separate
family_note: The README describes both standalone and integrated versions. The grant recorded is limited to the application code in sprint-flows; external document repositories, signature services, integration targets and separately published libraries are not relicensed by this entry. CNR's publiccode landingURL maps this exact repo to the current Nuova Scrivania Digitale service.
status_note: The first root LICENSE/source grant commit is dated 2019-12-04. Last substantive source/UI change observed was 2023-04-18; subsequent 2025 dependency/POM and 2026 CI changes are not counted as application-feature commits. The CNR landingURL, live service, 2025 system-wide notice, and current 2026 call demonstrate ongoing official operation and source/product identity, meeting the maintained exception. publiccode releaseDate was not used as the source year.

decision_reason: CNR-IIT developed STI under AgID-CNR FSE conventions and its multi-repository source is publicly accessible, but hold because exact first-party grant/scope is contradictory across the source modules and there is no current product-specific use/support evidence for source that has been unchanged since March 2022. The CNR host timed out during this review; I do not infer product failure from that transient access result.

government_provenance.note: CNR's institutional 2024 final-project-report record says STI source was developed by CNR-IIT under earlier AgID-CNR conventions and describes the later AgID-CNR source-release/reuse work for public administrations. This directly documents public sponsorship and product-specific development.

public_source.note: The assigned CNR repository is a public product-description/metadata umbrella that names three linked module repositories; the linked portlets/build, service, and CTS2-framework repositories expose the actual source and build/install guidance without credentials. The code is distributed across those repos rather than contained in the assigned docs-only root.

eligible_license.note: The assigned publiccode.yml and umbrella LICENSE assert GPL-3.0-or-later/GPLv3, and the STI service/portlets READMEs likewise claim GPL-3.0-or-later; however, both of those component repositories contain Apache-2.0 LICENSE files, while the separately required CTS2 framework repo also contains Apache-2.0 and describes Mayo Clinic's framework. Exact first-party grant boundaries across the integrated product cannot be determined from the conflicting source notices.

primary_evidence.note: The public abstract for CNR's 2024 final project report describes open-source release and experimentation, but the attached report is restricted and does not let me verify current deployment/source parity. All three linked source repos have latest commits by 2022-03-15; the official STI host did not respond before timeout on 2026-09-29, so continuing deployment, distribution/support, and recent use remain unverified.

product_identity: STI (Servizio Terminologico Integrato), CNR-IIT's integrated terminology service for regional/health-information systems and FSE coding sets
agency: Consiglio Nazionale delle Ricerche, Istituto di Informatica e Telematica (CNR-IIT), developed under public collaboration/conventions with Agenzia per l'Italia Digitale (AgID)
geography: Italy; CNR-IIT development at Arcavacata di Rende, Calabria, under a national CNR-AgID collaboration headquartered in Rome
license: Unresolved mixed scope: assigned STI publiccode/umbrella README assert GPL-3.0-or-later, but two CNR component repos carry Apache-2.0 LICENSE files and matching README GPL claims; CTS2 framework is separately Apache-2.0. Do not attribute one product-wide grant until each first-party component's governing notice is clarified.
family_note: The assigned CNR STI URL is a product-description/metadata umbrella repository, with no application source files. Its README names three source modules: `iit-rende/sti-cts2-framework`, `iit-rende/sti-service`, and `iit-rende/sti-cts2-portlets-build`; the canonical_repository_url points to the portlets/front-end module only and is not a complete system. The framework README identifies it as Mayo Clinic's CTS2 implementation, so its Apache grant is separate from CNR STI integration code.
status_note: The first public commits carrying source/license material in the linked STI modules are dated 2021-09-13; the assigned umbrella repo's root license appears in March 2022, and the linked repositories' last observed code commits are 2022-03-15. CNR's 2024 IRIS record documents an official source-release/reuse project but the report file is restricted; current source-to-live-service correspondence and maintenance are not established. The 2021 open-source year is based on module commit history, not publiccode releaseDate.
